steps.name: Paired DESeq2 DE: treated vs control blocking on subject
caveats: With 4 residual df, dispersion estimation is shaky and a null-looking p-value histogram is a plausible, honest outcome — report it as such rather than lowering thresholds to manufacture hits.

steps.context: Human whole-blood bulk RNA-seq, 5 subjects each sampled under control and treated conditions. constraints: Design must be ~ subject + condition with subject as a factor — never a condition-only design.

Match count matrix columns to metadata sample IDs by name and reorder; fail loudly on any mismatch rather than assuming column order.

Report both unshrunken log2FC (for the test statistic) and apeglm-shrunken log2FC (for ranking) in the same table.
Report the low-count filter used and the number of genes retained from the 12,000 input genes.

steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-without-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 gene symbols x 10 sample columns, raw integer counts from STAR/featureCounts) and /eval-full-32-without-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (10 rows; columns for sample, subject, condition). steps.name: Cross-method concordance and per-subject response consistency
caveats: High cross-method concordance is expected simply because all three share the same counts and design — it is a sanity check, not independent replication. Say so.
Per-subject ratios on a single replicate per cell carry no within-cell error estimate; they describe consistency, they do not test it.
A gene whose pooled significance vanishes when one subject is dropped should be reported as fragile, not as a finding.
steps.context: At 5 pairs, a single discordant subject can create or destroy a hit. Method concordance guards against distributional-assumption artefacts, and the per-subject ratio / leave-one-subject-out view is the most direct answer to 'which genes respond within each subject' — it distinguishes a consistent treatment response from a one-subject outlier that survived pooling.
steps.question: Do limma-voom and edgeR paired models agree with DESeq2 on the treated-vs-control genes, and is each candidate gene's response consistent across all 5 subjects rather than driven by one pair?
constraints: All three models must use the identical gene filter and the identical paired design matrix as T1S1 — no re-filtering with different rules.
Per-subject log2 ratios must be computed on DESeq2 normalized counts (or edgeR CPM) with an explicit pseudocount, and the pseudocount stated.
Leave-one-subject-out must be reported for every gene in the reported candidate set, with the range of the effect estimate across the 5 leave-out fits.
If no gene reaches padj<0.1 in any method, do not lower the FDR bar as if it were significance — report the top-ranked genes explicitly labelled as non-significant candidates.
Direction consistency must be counted out of 5 subjects and reported per gene.
steps.description: Using the same filtered count matrix and the same paired design (~ subject + condition) from T1S1, refit the contrast two further ways: (1) limma-voom with the explicit subject-blocked design matrix and eBayes, and (2) edgeR with TMM normalization, estimateDisp on the paired design, glmQLFit/glmQLFTest. A per-subject log2 ratio matrix (candidate genes x 5 subjects) with a direction-consistency count and a single-subject-driven flag per gene.
Leave-one-subject-out effect ranges reported for every candidate gene.
A heatmap of per-subject log2 ratios for the candidate gene set.
Explicit labelling of whether the candidate set is FDR-significant or merely top-ranked.

steps.name: Preranked pathway enrichment of the paired treatment contrast
caveats: GSEA on a ranking derived from a 4-residual-df model inherits that instability; treat enriched sets as hypotheses, not established mechanism.

Blood expression is strongly driven by cell-composition shifts — an enriched immune-cell-associated set may reflect a change in leukocyte proportions rather than transcriptional regulation within a cell type. Say this in the interpretation.
Hallmark and GO sets overlap heavily with one another; do not present concordance between the two collections as independent corroboration.
steps.context: Whole blood treatment response is typically expressed as coordinated shifts in interferon, inflammatory, and cell-cycle programmes rather than a handful of large single-gene effects, so a set-level readout can be informative when gene-level FDR is not. The environment's reference store carries human MSigDB hallmark, human GO BP/CC/MF, and human WikiPathways gene sets, all keyed on HGNC symbols, which matches the gene-symbol row identifiers of counts.csv.
steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark states are coordinately shifted by treatment in whole blood, based on the ranking of the full paired treated-vs-control contrast?
constraints: Use the HUMAN gene set collections — the store also holds mouse and rat versions and using them on this Homo sapiens data would produce meaningless results.
Rank on the full filtered gene list from T1S1, not on a thresholded significant subset.
State which ranking statistic was used and set a fixed random seed for fgsea permutations.
Restrict to gene sets with between 15 and 500 members present in the tested gene universe, and report the universe size.
Collapse redundant GO terms (parent/child sharing most members) before quoting a count of significant processes.
Annotate each significant set's leading-edge genes with the per-subject consistency flags from T1S2.
If the gene set files are absent at run time, report the absence explicitly and emit the ranked list only — do not substitute a different organism's sets or an internet download.
steps.description: Take the complete gene-level result table from T1S1 (all filtered genes, human HGNC symbols) and run preranked gene set enrichment (fgsea) on a ranking built from the DESeq2 statistic — use the Wald stat, or sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue), and state which was used. Optionally also test the human WikiPathways collection if present. Report the leading-edge genes for each significant set and cross-reference them against the per-subject consistency flags from T1S2, so a pathway driven by genes that were single-subject artefacts is marked as such. Collapse redundant parent/child GO terms before reporting a count. If neither hallmark nor GO gene sets are available in the environment, report that plainly and fall back to reporting the ranked gene list alone — the DE result from T1S1/T1S2 remains the answer to the research question without this step.
acceptance_criteria: A preranked GSEA result table per collection with NES, p-value, FDR, set size and leading-edge genes.
Explicit statement of the ranking statistic, the gene universe size, the set-size bounds, and the seed.
Leading-edge genes cross-referenced to the T1S2 per-subject consistency flags.
GO redundancy collapsed before any count of significant terms is reported.
If reference gene sets are unavailable, an explicit statement of that fact rather than a silent organism substitution.

plan.title: Paired treated-vs-control blood RNA-seq DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The data are raw integer gene-level counts (12,000 gene symbols x 10 sample columns, star_featurecounts) from human whole blood, with a metadata table of 10 samples carrying subject and condition. The design is explicitly paired: 5 subjects, each contributing one control and one treated sample. The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is exactly a paired two-condition differential expression problem, and the paired structure must be modelled (~ subject + condition) rather than ignored, because between-subject expression variance in blood is large relative to a treatment effect and an unpaired test on n=5+5 would be badly underpowered and confounded by subject identity.

T1S1 runs the primary DE with DESeq2 using the design ~ subject + condition, on genes passing a low-count filter (edgeR::filterByExpr with the paired design, or a manual >=10 counts in >=5 samples rule). Blocking on subject consumes 4 residual degrees of freedom, leaving 4 for the condition effect, so the analysis is honestly underpowered — that must be reported alongside the results, not buried. LFC shrinkage (apeglm) is applied for ranking, but unshrunken values are reported for the statistics. QC diagnostics (library sizes, VST PCA coloured by subject and by condition, sample-sample correlation) come out of the same step to confirm that subject dominates the first principal component, which is the empirical justification for the paired model.

T1S2 is a robustness check rather than a new claim: the same paired contrast run with limma-voom with duplicateCorrelation-free explicit subject blocking, plus edgeR paired glmQLFit. Concordance of the three methods on the significant set is the evidence that a hit is real, not a modelling artefact at n=5. It also computes per-subject log2 ratios (treated vs control per subject, on normalized counts) so the question 'within each subject' is answered directly and consistency across subjects can be inspected gene by gene — a gene driven by one subject is flagged.

T1S3 places the resulting ranked gene list into biological context using the staged human hallmark and GO gene sets against the shrunken-LFC ranking (fgsea preranked, which is appropriate when few genes clear FDR). It is annotation, not a claim of mechanism, and will report explicitly if the ranked list is too weak to support enrichment.
